sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 On 08.03.2024 at about 07.30 p.m, the petitioner was riding his Bullet Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-07-EE-1410 along with one Ramcharan as a pillion rider from Balasandra towards T.Gollahalli and while so proceeding near Sangasandra Gate, the pillion rider asked to stop the vehicle for attending nature call, the petitioner stopped his Motor Cycle on the side of the road and at that time a Crane/Construction equipment vehicle bearing No.KA-07-N-6265 came from their behind at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to this the petitioner fell down along with Motor Cycle and sustained grievous injuries and his Motor Cycle was also damaged and immediately he was shifted to R.L.
Jalappa hospital, Kolar and after initial treatment, he was taken to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein the doctors was not available and hence, the petitioner was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 09.03.2024 to 11.04.2024 and has undergone surgery and has spent Rs.18,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, medicines,
conveyance, nourishment, attendance charges etc., and the Motor Cycle was damaged in the said accident to an extent of Rs.25,000/- and prior to (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged 28 years and was working as SAGr-11 at Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd., Mulabagal and drawing salary of Rs.48,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is permanently disabled and not in a position to attend the work and lost his income.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Crane/Construction equipment vehicle driver and in this regard the Mulabagal Rural Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending vehicle.

Hence, the respondents No.1 being the R.C. Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, they were placed exparte.

04. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Points that arise for my consideration:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION Chalapathi P vs Srinivasa S on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966486/

2 01. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.03.2024 at about 07.30 p.m, (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 near Sangasandra Gate, Ramasandra Road, Mulabagal Taluk,
Kolar District, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Crane/Construction equipment vehicle bearing No.KA-07-N-6265 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

05. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined three witnesses as PW.2 to 4 and through them got marked 32 documents as Ex.P.1 to 32 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
Since respondents have placed exparte, respondents did not lead their evidence.
06. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the records.

07. My findings on the above Points are as follows:
 Point No.1 In the Affirmative  Point No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Point No.3

As per final order  for the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3518/2024  REASONS 08.
Point No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
But despite of service of notice, the respondents have remained absent and placed exparte.
Hence, whatever oral evidence adduced by the PW.1 is remains unchallenged and uncontravented.

There is no oath against oath and there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1.
09.

Further, PW.2 is MRD Assistant at Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru and he has produced MLC extract, Police intimation, original Inpatient case sheet and X-rays of the petitioner as per Ex.P.23 to 26.
His evidence is also remains unchallenged and uncontravented.

10. Further, PW.3 is Junior Executive Officer at R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar, he has produced MLC extract, Police intimation and OPD book of the petitioner as per Ex.P.28 to 30 and his evidence is also remains unchallenged and uncontravented.

Further, PW.4 is a Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated in his chief-examination evidence that the (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 petitioner has sustained left lower limb crush injury with partial tendon tear with medial retinaculam tear and he assessed permanent physical disability of 50% of left lower limb, which is 25% of whole body and he has produced OPD card and X-ray of the petitioner as per Ex.P.31 and 32.

His evidence is also remains unchallenged and uncontravented and there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1 to 4.
12.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 32 documents as Ex.P.1 to 32 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Mulbagal Rural Police against the driver of the offending Crane.

Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against driver of the offending Crane for his rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle who caused the accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Statement of petitioner.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Statement of eye-witness.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV report which discloses involvement of both vehicles in the alleged accident and Motor Cycle of the petitioner was heavily damaged.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Wound certificate which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.8 is Discharge card of R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar, which shows that the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 petitioner was admitted as inpatient on 08.03.2024 for one day due to accidental injuries.

Ex. P.9 is the Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital on 09.03.2024 and discharged on 11.04.2024 totally for 34 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.15 is Medical investigation reports.

Ex.P.16 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Crane and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Crane and caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.21 is Photographs of the injured parts of the petitioner.

13. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, which clearly establishes that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.03.2024 at about 07.30 p.m, near Sangasandra Gate, Ramasandra Road,
Mulabagal (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 Taluk, Kolar District, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Crane/Construction equipment vehicle bearing No.KA-07-N-6265, by its driver, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Point No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was aged 28 years and was working as SAGr-11 at Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd.,
Mulabagal and drawing salary of Rs.48,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.18,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, medicines, conveyance, nourishment, attendance charges etc.,.

sentences.text: It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.10 Aadhaar card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.05.1995.
The alleged (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 accident occurred on 08.03.2024.
Eventhough said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age, but in the absence of evidence regarding other documents, this document can be relied upon.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 29 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 29 years as on the date of accident.
As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case

With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.11
Notarized copy of ID Card issued by KPTCL, Ex.P.12 Pay slip for the month of December 2023, January 2024 and February 2024, Ex
.P.17 Notarized copy of offer of appointment and Ex.P.18 Letter issued by KPTCL dt:07.11.2024 regarding sanction of medical advance amount.
Since the petitioner is employee under KPTCL which is Government Corporation, it is not necessary to examine the employer of the said Corporation.
Therefore, said documents can be relied upon so far as avocation and income of petitioner is concerned.
Therefore, according to Ex.P.12 Salary certificate, (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 petitioner has get gross salary of Rs.48,600/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.48,000/-.
17.

According to the evidence of PW.4, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained left lower limb crush injury with partial tendon tear with medial retinaculam tear and he assessed permanent physical disability of 50% of left lower limb, which is 25% of whole body.
Hence, considering the evidence of PW.4 and nature of injuries sustained and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 17%.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.8 and 9 Discharge summaries the petitioner was admitted at R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, as inpatient for nearly 34 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.50,000/- under this head.
19. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.4 doctor and Ex.P.15 Medical investigation reports, Ex.P.25 Original inpatient case sheet, Ex.P.26 and 32 are X-rays, Ex.P.30 OPD book and Ex.P.31 OPD card and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.50,000/- under this Chalapathi P vs Srinivasa S on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966486/
5 head.
20. Loss of income during

As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.48,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for nearly 34 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast four months.

Thus,
taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.1,92,000/-
(Rs.48,000 x 4) under this head.
(SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 21. Medical expenses:- As per Ex.P.14 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.9,47,957/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,47,957/- under this head.

22. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
23. Future medical expenses:- The petitioner has not produced any evidence regarding future medical expenses and PW.4 doctor has not stated anything about future medical expenses of the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.
24. Repair charges:-
The petitioner has stated that due to accident his Motor Cycle was heavily damaged and has produced Ex.P.20 Service estimation.
But petitioner has not examined the author of Ex.P.20.
Hence, said document cannot be relied upon and petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

sentences.text: Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.29,54,597/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

27. The petitioner has relied upon following citations in support of his claim:-
01. 2007 ACJ 210 02. 2011 ACJ 1971 03. 2012 ACJ 2694 04. 2005 ACJ 644 (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 I have gone through the above citations and same are taken into consideration while awarding compensation.
28. Regarding liability:- As discussed earlier, despite service of summons to the respondents No.1 and 2, they remained absent and placed exparte.

According to averments made in the petition, the offending vehicle had insurance policy bearing No:3380/02175971/000/01 which is valid from 08.07.2023 to 07.07.2024 and even the Police have not filed Charge sheet against owner or driver of the offending vehicle for driving the vehicle without insurance policy and even respondent No.2 has not denied existence of insurance policy.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.29,54,597/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Point No.2 partly in affirmative.
29. Point No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,54,597/- (Rupees Twenty nine lakhs fifty four thousand five hundred and ninety seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of Chalapathi P vs Srinivasa S on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966486/
7 three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.29,54,597/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3518/2024 deposit.
29. Point No.3:
In view of reasons assigned to Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,54,597/- (Rupees Twenty nine lakhs fifty four thousand five hundred and ninety seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
